newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH KLM SOOTHES PASSENGER RADIOACTIVITY FEARS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH KLM SOOTHES PASSENGER RADIOACTIVITY FEARS.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM on Sunday soothed fears that passengers on one of its London-bound flights in May might have been exposed to excessive doses of radiation from a cargo of medical equipment.

Britain's Observer newspaper earlier reported that an inspection of the cargo by British aviation authorities had indicated slightly higher levels of radiation than that shown on the equipment packaging.
But a KLM spokeswoman said that the radioactivity of the cargo on its May 2 KL129 flight had at no time exceeded Dutch or European safety norms.
"There was absolutely no cause for concern, given that the actual levels of radiation (found by British and Dutch inspectors) were well below any legal norms or limits," Marjolein Wenting said.
"For this reason we did not consider it necessary to inform the passengers," she said.
